findings.property: The interpreter script input must be a directly pinned regular file, including when the approved interpreter path is resolved.
findings.evidence: scripts/task-run-guard.py:192-196 recognizes only the literal /usr/bin/python3 for Python script-position validation. However pin() at 72-75 forbids symlink paths, and /usr/bin/python3 resolves to /usr/bin/python3.12 in this review environment; tests/contract/workflow/task_run_guard_test.py:48-50 accordingly pins and executes the resolved path. An action argv of [resolved_python, directory] skips script_index validation. The initial isfile loop ignores directories and the later loop explicitly permits them at 215-216. Python executes directory/__main__.py, whose bytes and mode are not required in candidate pins. All postvalidation repeats the same omission. This permits an executable program input to escape the exact regular-source pin contract. Source analysis only; no additional runtime probe was authorized or executed.
findings.falsifier: Before any further authorized source repair, preserve a focused behavioral regression using the resolved system Python and a temporary directory containing a harmless marker __main__.py that is absent from candidates. Require refusal 78 before attempt/dispatch and marker absence; retain a healthy directly pinned regular-script control. Ensure interpreter identification and script-position validation apply to the resolved executable form actually allowed by pin admission.
